story.what_it_does: NMDC is India's largest iron ore producer, mining a record 53.15 million tonnes in FY26 and selling about 502 lakh tonnes. It also has smaller coal and steel-related activities, though the Benga coal mine produced nothing in FY26.
story.plans: Management targets 60 million tonnes of production in FY27 and 100 million tonnes of capacity by FY30. It expects capex of about ₹6,000 crore in FY27, up from a record ~₹3,300 crore in FY26, and aims to keep the iron ore EBITDA margin near 42%.
story.moat: Its scale as the country's largest iron ore miner and its record output are the main strengths in the notes. However, major customers JSW and AM-NS have bought captive mines and may shift away from NMDC ore, and the notes give no other protective advantages.

scenarios.story: Output reaches 60 million tonnes in FY27 as new mines ramp up, and the iron ore margin holds near 42%. Capex spending then builds toward the 100 million tonne goal.
signals_to_watch: Q1 FY27 production of 5.3 million tonnes versus 4.4 million a year earlier continuing through the year
Iron ore standalone EBITDA margin staying around 42%

scenarios.story: Production and sales grow steadily, but realisations stay lower than a year ago and costs stay high, so margins land somewhat below the best levels. Growth beyond 60 million tonnes depends on railway doubling and clearances arriving on time.
signals_to_watch: Average domestic realisation per tonne (₹4,759 in Q4 FY26, down 5% year on year)
Doubling of the KK railway line by October 2026

scenarios.story: Big customers move to their own mines, and the retrospective Karnataka mineral tax and slow recovery of dues from NMDC Steel and RINL strain the finances. Delays in clearances or rising costs could also hold back growth.
signals_to_watch: Karnataka mineral tax bill (₹15,481.72 crore contingent liability) and presidential assent
Recovery of dues from NMDC Steel (₹1,851.39 crore) and RINL (₹4,586.31 crore)
